az_jungle_the.blurb: A small bouldering wall of two stacked cliff bands tucked up a wash on the Bear Canyon side of Mount Lemmon, above the Catalina Highway near Tucson. Twelve problems climb the dark and tan streaked granite, running from VB-level easy up through the V7 range. The grades lean toward the middle and upper end, with a fair share of V4 and V5 and one hard problem at the top, so it suits boulderers past the beginner stage. The wall picks up shade around midday in spring, and the walk in is short but leaves the main trail and follows a wash, so expect some route finding.
az_jungle_the.parking_note: Use the roadside pullout near mile 9.7 to 9.8 on the Catalina Highway, marked by a yellow 20 mph sign. The same pullout serves the neighbouring boulders in this canyon.

az_lost_hawk.blurb: Lost Hawk is a pinnacle in Bear Canyon, a short walk from the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon outside Tucson. Twelve routes mix sport lines with a few trad climbs, and the bulk sit in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a couple of easier leads and a single route in the 5.11 range. That makes it a friendly stop for newer leaders and a quick half-day for anyone cragging along the highway. The pinnacle is compact, the approach is brief and involves a short drainage descent, and it sits in a canyon known for shade among pines lower on the mountain.

az_mariposita.blurb: Mariposita is an easy-to-reach sport crag on the upper Catalina Highway of Mount Lemmon, at roughly 7,450 feet. All twelve routes are bolted, with a couple of easy 5.7 lines, a handful of 5.9 to 5.10 climbs, and a few 5.11 and low 5.12 pitches at the top end. The stone has an unusual texture, with loose pieces and dense sections, so test holds and wear a helmet. Afternoons bring shade, and the shade comes sooner in winter as the sun drops south. The walk starts from the Butterfly Trail and takes about a quarter hour.
az_mariposita.parking_note: Park in the Butterfly Trail lot on the right just before the next signed lot along the highway, then follow the trail down toward the crag.

az_knights_wall.blurb: Knights Wall is a steep sport crag in the Windy Ridge zone of Mount Lemmon, at about 6,700 feet along the Catalina Highway. Most of its twelve routes are around 70 to 90 feet on vertical to overhanging stone, and nearly all are hard: the bulk fall in the 5.12 range, backed by a few 5.10s, one 5.11 and a pair of 5.13s, with a couple of trad lines among them. It sits in a gully that stays cold and shady through most of the day, a contrast with the sunnier crags nearby. The short descent to the base has loose rock and debris.

az_sloth_slab.blurb: Sloth Slab is a beginner-oriented sport crag high on Mount Lemmon, near 7,800 feet in the Upper Highway zone. The slab starts low-angle, with some lines steepening into a juggy, near-vertical stretch. Of the twelve bolted routes, most are 5.6 or easier, a few reach 5.7 to 5.9, and one tops out around 5.10. The face points west and gets sun by late morning, so it is cooler in the early hours. Since some lines start from a ledge, a longer rope helps. High elevation means cold weather in winter and good relief from valley heat in summer.
